dataset.name: HD-EPIC
dataset.license_or_access_note: Existing user-confirmed research permission. No public release.

observed_events.description: A deep-bowled ladle is used to stir the soup in the same saucepan.
Food-processor parts are rinsed under the tap away from the hob; no requested utensil-soup relation is exposed.
A cleaning cloth is rinsed and squeezed at the sink, not used in the soup.
The open cutlery drawer and a newly taken spoon are visible. The held pan is empty; the old ladle is not actively in it.
A small oval-head table spoon scrapes the remaining soup from the same saucepan into a storage container.

supported_claims.text: Actual near sequence supports the physical referents and relation described in the oracle; no unobservable retail identity is required.

screening.real_user_need: I want an extra of one of the handheld kitchen utensils I used in the soup here. Add a product containing only that basic utensil type to my cart; a same-type multipack is fine. Brand, size, colour and material can differ.
screening.scope_note: Experiment-only Span content; identical resolved physical reference supplied upfront in both conditions. Not a new formal member.

construct.research_question: Can the Agent bind the same physical reference when two real intervening events lie between deciding observations?
construct.belief_before: More than one physical referent is plausible without the user reference.
construct.belief_after: The complete physical relation selects the same real category in both conditions.
construct.required_behavior_change: Connect the source events and choose one matching website offer.
construct.no_update_failure: The same oracle is supplied upfront; missing proactive clarification is not a confound.
construct.overupdate_failure: Adding an alternate object or extra package violates the final request.
construct.visual_dependency_claim: The user supplies a physical relation, not a website item name. Both roles have genuine public listings. Endpoint/background shortcut checks remain for independent review.
